plate_tectonics.name: angular_speed
plate_tectonics.title: Euler-pole angular speed
plate_tectonics.why: Rigid plate motion is rotation about an Euler pole.
plate_tectonics.limit: Constant angular rate; angular input is radians and output radians per second.

plate_tectonics.name: plate_speed
plate_tectonics.title: Rigid plate speed about an Euler pole
plate_tectonics.why: Distance from the rotation axis controls surface plate speed.
plate_tectonics.limit: Spherical rigid plate, magnitude only; angular distance must be at most pi.

plate_tectonics.name: euler_velocity_x
plate_tectonics.title: Euler rotation east-fixed x velocity
plate_tectonics.why: The cross product of rotation and position gives Cartesian plate velocity.
plate_tectonics.limit: Earth-fixed Cartesian axes; x is not the local east component.

plate_tectonics.name: euler_velocity_y
plate_tectonics.title: Euler rotation y velocity
plate_tectonics.why: A rigid plate velocity field is tangent to its spherical path.
plate_tectonics.limit: Same Earth-fixed Cartesian convention as euler_velocity_x.

plate_tectonics.name: euler_velocity_z
plate_tectonics.title: Euler rotation polar velocity
plate_tectonics.why: The polar velocity component completes the Euler-vector cross product.
plate_tectonics.limit: Earth-fixed components, not local vertical motion or deformation.

plate_tectonics.name: plate_displacement
plate_tectonics.title: Plate kinematic displacement
plate_tectonics.why: Velocity connects short instrumental records with geological displacement.
plate_tectonics.limit: Constant signed speed along a local coordinate; not a finite Euler rotation.

plate_tectonics.name: spreading_age
plate_tectonics.title: Magnetic-stripe spreading clock
plate_tectonics.why: Symmetric ocean-floor ages link ridge spreading to plate creation.
plate_tectonics.limit: Distance on one side and half-spreading rate; changes in rate are omitted.

plate_tectonics.name: full_spreading_rate
plate_tectonics.title: Symmetric full spreading rate
plate_tectonics.why: Opposite plate velocities combine into ridge opening speed.
plate_tectonics.limit: Symmetric spreading; asymmetric velocities require their own relative-vector calculation.

plate_tectonics.name: convergence_rate
plate_tectonics.title: Signed plate-boundary convergence
plate_tectonics.why: Resolving relative motion normal to a boundary separates convergence and shear.
plate_tectonics.limit: Positive normal component denotes convergence; negative denotes divergence.

plate_tectonics.name: fault_slip_rate
plate_tectonics.title: Tangential boundary slip rate
plate_tectonics.why: The tangential motion component connects oblique convergence to strike slip.
plate_tectonics.limit: Supplied obliquity is oriented from the positive convergence normal.

plate_tectonics.name: subduction_travel_time
plate_tectonics.title: Slab path travel time
plate_tectonics.why: Slab dip changes the path length required to reach a specified depth.
plate_tectonics.limit: Straight slab at constant speed; zero dip cannot reach depth and is rejected.

plate_tectonics.name: slab_pull_force
plate_tectonics.title: Slab negative-buoyancy force
plate_tectonics.why: A cold slab can drive motion through its excess weight.
plate_tectonics.limit: Simple buoyancy force magnitude; drag, phase changes and mantle flow are excluded.

plate_tectonics.name: airy_root
plate_tectonics.title: Airy crustal compensation
plate_tectonics.why: Crustal buoyancy provides a baseline for mountain-root support.
plate_tectonics.limit: Local compensation without plate flexure; mantle must be denser than crust.
plate_tectonics.extra: require(mantle_density > crust_density, "mantle must be denser than crust")

plate_tectonics.name: flexural_rigidity
plate_tectonics.title: Elastic lithosphere rigidity
plate_tectonics.why: Elastic thickness turns lithospheric strength into a bending resistance.
plate_tectonics.limit: Thin isotropic elastic plate with stable Poisson ratio, not a yielding viscoelastic lithosphere.

plate_tectonics.name: flexural_parameter
plate_tectonics.title: Lithosphere flexural length
plate_tectonics.why: Bending and buoyancy jointly set the scale of load compensation.
plate_tectonics.limit: Infinite beam-like plate convention alpha to the fourth equals 4D over density contrast times g.

plate_tectonics.name: halfspace_temperature
plate_tectonics.title: Cooling oceanic lithosphere
plate_tectonics.why: Oceanic plates cool as their age and distance from a ridge increase.
plate_tectonics.limit: Semi-infinite conduction with fixed surface temperature; no hydrothermal or advective heat transfer.
plate_tectonics.extra: require(mantle_temperature >= surface_temperature, "mantle must be at least as warm as surface")

plate_tectonics.name: halfspace_heat_flux
plate_tectonics.title: Cooling-plate surface heat flux
plate_tectonics.why: Surface heat flux decreases as an oceanic plate cools.
plate_tectonics.limit: Positive upward flux; semi-infinite conductive model excludes the zero-age singularity.
plate_tectonics.extra: require(mantle_temperature >= surface_temperature, "mantle must be at least as warm as surface")

plate_tectonics.name: mantle_rayleigh_number
plate_tectonics.title: Rayleigh number of a convecting mantle layer
plate_tectonics.expr: thermal_expansivity * density * gravity * temperature_difference * thickness**3 / (diffusivity * viscosity)
plate_tectonics.why: Buoyancy against viscous and thermal diffusion decides whether the mantle convects.
plate_tectonics.limit: Layer heated from below with uniform properties; convection starts above about 657.5 (free slip) or 1708 (rigid walls).

plate_tectonics.name: flexural_deflection
plate_tectonics.title: Elastic plate deflection under a line load
plate_tectonics.expr: line_load * alpha**3 / (8 * rigidity) * np.exp(-abs(distance) / alpha) * (np.cos(abs(distance) / alpha) + np.sin(abs(distance) / alpha))
plate_tectonics.why: A load bends the lithosphere into a moat flanked by a peripheral bulge.
plate_tectonics.limit: Unbroken infinite thin elastic plate, deflection positive downward; density contrast is mantle minus infill.

plate_tectonics.name: hotspot_age
plate_tectonics.title: Age progression along a hotspot track
plate_tectonics.why: A plate moving over a fixed plume leaves volcanoes that age with distance along a small circle.
plate_tectonics.limit: Fixed hotspot and constant Euler rotation of the plate over it; track length is measured along the small circle.

plate_tectonics.name: ocean_depth
plate_tectonics.title: Ocean depth of a cooling half-space
plate_tectonics.expr: ridge_depth + 2 * mantle_density * thermal_expansivity * (mantle_temperature - surface_temperature) / (mantle_density - water_density) * np.sqrt(diffusivity * age / np.pi)
plate_tectonics.why: Thermal contraction of the cooling plate makes the sea floor deepen with the square root of its age.
plate_tectonics.limit: Isostatic half-space cooling, depth positive downward; it overestimates depth on sea floor older than about 70 million years.
plate_tectonics.extra: require(mantle_density > water_density, "mantle must be denser than water"); require(mantle_temperature >= surface_temperature, "mantle must be at least as warm as surface")

plate_tectonics.name: compose_euler_vectors
plate_tectonics.title: Composition of relative Euler vectors around a plate circuit
plate_tectonics.why: Angular velocities of rigid plates add, so two relative motions predict the third.
plate_tectonics.limit: Instantaneous rotations only; inputs and output have three Cartesian components on the last axis.
plate_tectonics.extra: require(omega_ab.shape[-1] == 3 and omega_bc.shape[-1] == 3, "three Cartesian components on the last axis")

seismology.name: p_wave_speed
seismology.title: Compressional-wave elasticity
seismology.why: Elastic moduli and density determine compressional wave speed.
seismology.limit: Homogeneous isotropic small-strain medium; shear modulus may vanish in a fluid.

seismology.name: s_wave_speed
seismology.title: Shear-wave elasticity
seismology.why: Shear waves reveal rigidity and disappear in an ideal fluid.
seismology.limit: Homogeneous isotropic medium; zero shear modulus returns zero speed.

seismology.name: poisson_ratio
seismology.title: Elastic velocity ratio
seismology.why: Wave-speed ratios constrain isotropic elastic response.
seismology.limit: Requires positive bulk modulus: vp squared must exceed 4 vs squared over 3.
seismology.extra: require(p_speed**2 > 4 * s_speed**2 / 3, "wave speeds imply nonpositive bulk modulus")

seismology.name: travel_time
seismology.title: Homogeneous travel time
seismology.why: Arrival times connect source distance and propagation speed.
seismology.limit: Straight path in a homogeneous medium; not a ray tracer.

seismology.name: seismic_impedance
seismology.title: Acoustic impedance
seismology.why: Impedance contrasts control normal-incidence reflection.
seismology.limit: Scalar acoustic impedance; elastic mode conversion is excluded.

seismology.name: reflection_coefficient
seismology.title: Normal-incidence pressure reflection
seismology.why: An interface divides incident energy into reflected and transmitted waves.
seismology.limit: Pressure amplitude convention at normal incidence; coefficient can be negative.

seismology.name: transmission_coefficient
seismology.title: Normal-incidence pressure transmission
seismology.why: Pressure transmission differs from transmitted energy fraction.
seismology.limit: Normal-incidence acoustic pressure amplitudes, not displacement amplitudes.

seismology.name: critical_angle
seismology.title: Snell refraction critical angle
seismology.why: Snell refraction explains head waves above a faster layer.
seismology.limit: Incidence from the slower medium; second speed must exceed first.
seismology.extra: require(speed2 > speed1, "second medium must be faster")

seismology.name: seismic_moment
seismology.title: Fault seismic moment
seismology.why: Moment connects an earthquake to fault area and displacement.
seismology.limit: Scalar mean-slip estimate; no spatial rupture distribution.

seismology.name: moment_magnitude
seismology.title: Moment magnitude in SI
seismology.why: Moment magnitude relates logarithmic event size to scalar moment.
seismology.limit: Uses the 9.1 intercept with moment in N m, not dyne cm.

seismology.name: moment_from_magnitude
seismology.title: Inverse moment magnitude
seismology.why: Inverting magnitude enables comparisons on a physical moment scale.
seismology.limit: Same SI convention as moment_magnitude; very large inputs can overflow.

seismology.name: gutenberg_richter
seismology.title: Earthquake frequency-size relation
seismology.why: A logarithmic frequency-size law summarizes an earthquake catalogue.
seismology.limit: Expected cumulative count for the fitted catalogue interval; completeness matters.

seismology.name: omori_rate
seismology.title: Modified Omori aftershock rate
seismology.why: Aftershock rates often decay with time after a main shock.
seismology.limit: Empirical fitted rate; no earthquake timing or location prediction.

seismology.name: ricker_wavelet
seismology.title: Ricker seismic source pulse
seismology.why: A compact pulse makes propagation and filtering examples inspectable.
seismology.limit: Unit peak at zero time; frequency is the peak-spectrum convention.

seismology.name: attenuated_amplitude
seismology.title: Constant-Q wave attenuation
seismology.why: Finite quality factor models intrinsic amplitude decay during propagation.
seismology.limit: Constant-Q narrowband attenuation; geometric spreading is separate.

seismology.name: rayleigh_wave_speed
seismology.title: Rayleigh surface-wave speed
seismology.why: A free surface guides a slower wave that combines compression and shear.
seismology.limit: Homogeneous isotropic half-space with a traction-free surface; requires positive bulk modulus.
seismology.extra: gamma = (s_speed / p_speed)**2; xi is the root in (0, 1) of xi**3 - 8 * xi**2 + (24 - 16 * gamma) * xi - 16 * (1 - gamma), found by bisection; require(p_speed**2 > 4 * s_speed**2 / 3, "wave speeds imply nonpositive bulk modulus")

seismology.name: head_wave_travel_time
seismology.title: Head-wave travel time below a single layer
seismology.expr: distance / speed2 + 2 * thickness * np.sqrt(speed2**2 - speed1**2) / (speed1 * speed2)
seismology.why: A wave critically refracted along a faster layer overtakes the direct wave at long range.
seismology.limit: Flat layer over a faster half-space, surface source and receiver; only beyond the critical distance.
seismology.extra: require(speed2 > speed1, "second medium must be faster"); require(distance >= 2 * thickness * speed1 / np.sqrt(speed2**2 - speed1**2), "distance is inside the critical distance")

seismology.name: crossover_distance
seismology.title: Head-wave crossover distance
seismology.why: The range at which the refracted wave arrives first measures the depth of the layer.
seismology.limit: Flat layer over a faster half-space; direct and head-wave times are equal there.
seismology.extra: require(speed2 > speed1, "second medium must be faster")

seismology.name: love_wave_angular_frequency
seismology.title: Fundamental Love-wave dispersion in a layer over a half-space
seismology.why: Shear waves trapped in a slow surface layer travel at a speed that depends on their period.
seismology.limit: Fundamental mode of a uniform layer over a faster uniform half-space; phase speed strictly between the two shear speeds.
seismology.extra: s1 = np.sqrt(phase_speed**2 / layer_s_speed**2 - 1); s2 = np.sqrt(1 - phase_speed**2 / halfspace_s_speed**2); require(phase_speed > layer_s_speed, "phase speed must exceed the layer shear speed"); require(phase_speed < halfspace_s_speed, "phase speed must be below the half-space shear speed")

seismology.name: ray_parameter
seismology.title: Ray parameter in a spherically layered Earth
seismology.why: Snell's law on a sphere keeps one quantity fixed along each ray, which fixes where it emerges.
seismology.limit: Spherically symmetric isotropic Earth; incidence angle from the radial direction, between 0 and pi/2.

seismology.name: local_magnitude
seismology.title: Richter local magnitude
seismology.why: A logarithm of recorded amplitude, corrected for distance, ranks earthquakes by size.
seismology.limit: Wood-Anderson amplitude and hypocentral distance; Hutton and Boore (1987) southern California correction for about 10 to 700 km.

seismology.name: vertical_travel_time
seismology.title: Vertical travel time through a tabulated speed profile
seismology.why: Integrating slowness through a reference Earth model predicts arrival times.
seismology.limit: Speed linear in depth between tabulated points; a repeated depth marks a discontinuity.
seismology.extra: require(depth.ndim == 1 and depth.size >= 2, "depth must be a vector with at least two samples"); require(speed.shape == depth.shape, "speed must have the same shape as depth"); require(np.all(np.diff(depth) >= 0), "depth must not decrease")

atmosphere.name: dry_air_density
atmosphere.title: Ideal-gas atmospheric density
atmosphere.why: An equation of state connects atmospheric pressure, temperature and density.
atmosphere.limit: Dry ideal air with fixed specific gas constant.

atmosphere.name: scale_height
atmosphere.title: Isothermal scale height
atmosphere.why: Hydrostatic balance predicts an exponential pressure scale.
atmosphere.limit: Dry isothermal atmosphere with constant gravity.

atmosphere.name: barometric_pressure
atmosphere.title: Isothermal barometric profile
atmosphere.why: Vertical pressure structure follows from hydrostatic balance and the gas law.
atmosphere.limit: Isothermal column; signed height is relative to the reference level.

atmosphere.name: potential_temperature
atmosphere.title: Poisson potential temperature
atmosphere.why: Adiabatic temperature adjustment permits comparisons across pressure levels.
atmosphere.limit: Dry ideal gas with constant heat capacity; not equivalent potential temperature.

atmosphere.name: temperature_from_potential
atmosphere.title: Inverse potential temperature
atmosphere.why: Potential-temperature inversion recovers the local dry-air temperature.
atmosphere.limit: Uses the same dry-air heat capacity and reference pressure convention.

atmosphere.name: dry_adiabatic_lapse_rate
atmosphere.title: Dry adiabatic lapse rate
atmosphere.why: Rising dry parcels cool as they perform expansion work.
atmosphere.limit: Returned positive lapse magnitude in K per metre; temperature decreases upward.

atmosphere.name: saturation_vapor_pressure
atmosphere.title: Integrated Clausius-Clapeyron approximation
atmosphere.why: Phase equilibrium makes saturation vapor pressure strongly temperature dependent.
atmosphere.limit: Liquid-water reference with constant latent heat; restricted to 180-330 K, not an ice saturation formula.

atmosphere.name: mixing_ratio
atmosphere.title: Water-vapor mass mixing ratio
atmosphere.why: Partial pressure determines water mass per unit dry-air mass.
atmosphere.limit: Ideal vapor mixture; vapor pressure must be below total pressure.
atmosphere.extra: require(vapor_pressure < total_pressure, "vapor pressure must be below total pressure")

atmosphere.name: specific_humidity
atmosphere.title: Specific humidity from mixing ratio
atmosphere.why: Changing the denominator connects two moisture conventions.
atmosphere.limit: Output is water mass per total moist-air mass.

atmosphere.name: virtual_temperature
atmosphere.title: Virtual-temperature buoyancy correction
atmosphere.why: Moist air is less dense than dry air at the same pressure and temperature.
atmosphere.limit: Ideal vapor mixture without suspended liquid or ice.

atmosphere.name: relative_humidity
atmosphere.title: Relative humidity fraction
atmosphere.why: Humidity compares actual vapor pressure to a saturation reference.
atmosphere.limit: Returned fraction may exceed one during supersaturation; no clipping.

atmosphere.name: coriolis_parameter
atmosphere.title: Rotating-Earth Coriolis parameter
atmosphere.why: Latitude controls rotational deflection and geophysical balance.
atmosphere.limit: Spherical rotating-Earth approximation; input is radians.

atmosphere.name: brunt_vaisala_squared
atmosphere.title: Dry static stability
atmosphere.why: A potential-temperature gradient determines dry stratification stability.
atmosphere.limit: Returns signed N squared; negative values represent instability rather than an imaginary frequency.

atmosphere.name: geostrophic_speed
atmosphere.title: Pressure-gradient geostrophic component
atmosphere.why: Pressure gradients and rotation can balance in large-scale flow.
atmosphere.limit: Signed cross-gradient component; invalid at the equator where coriolis vanishes.

atmosphere.name: rossby_number
atmosphere.title: Rossby dynamical scaling
atmosphere.why: Rossby number measures inertia relative to rotational effects.
atmosphere.limit: Magnitude scaling only; small values support but do not prove geostrophic balance.

atmosphere.name: barometer_column_height
atmosphere.title: Liquid barometer column height
atmosphere.why: The weight of a liquid column balances the pressure of the air above it.
atmosphere.limit: Incompressible liquid with a vacuum above the column; vapour pressure and capillarity are neglected.

atmosphere.name: two_layer_temperature
atmosphere.title: Troposphere-stratosphere temperature profile
atmosphere.why: Temperature falls with height up to the tropopause and stays constant above it.
atmosphere.limit: Constant-lapse troposphere under an isothermal lower stratosphere; the stratospheric warming above about 20 km is omitted.
atmosphere.extra: require(surface_temperature > lapse_rate * tropopause_height, "tropopause temperature must be positive")

atmosphere.name: richardson_number
atmosphere.title: Gradient Richardson number
atmosphere.why: Stratification suppresses the turbulence that vertical wind shear generates.
atmosphere.limit: Signed; stratified shear flow can become unstable only where it falls below 1/4 (Miles-Howard).

atmosphere.name: surface_pressure_tendency
atmosphere.title: Surface pressure tendency from column divergence
atmosphere.why: Mass leaving the column through net horizontal divergence lowers the surface pressure.
atmosphere.limit: Hydrostatic column with no surface mass flux; divergence at one level is far larger than the column mean.

atmosphere.name: rossby_wave_speed
atmosphere.title: Barotropic Rossby-wave zonal phase speed
atmosphere.why: The latitude gradient of the Coriolis parameter makes vorticity waves drift westward.
atmosphere.limit: Nondivergent barotropic flow on a beta plane; positive values are eastward.

climate.name: absorbed_solar
climate.title: Planetary mean absorbed sunlight
climate.why: Sphere geometry and reflection set the global mean solar input.
climate.limit: Global mean rather than local insolation; fixed bolometric albedo.

climate.name: effective_temperature
climate.title: Radiative equilibrium temperature
climate.why: Stefan-Boltzmann emission links an energy balance to temperature.
climate.limit: Single emitting level in equilibrium; not the surface temperature of a greenhouse atmosphere.

climate.name: outgoing_longwave
climate.title: Greybody infrared emission
climate.why: A greybody approximation maps temperature to outgoing radiant flux.
climate.limit: Constant emissivity; not a spectral atmospheric radiative-transfer solver.

climate.name: planck_feedback
climate.title: Blackbody restoring derivative
climate.why: The temperature derivative of emission supplies a radiative restoring coefficient.
climate.limit: Positive restoring magnitude in W per square metre per kelvin; other feedbacks are separate.

climate.name: co2_forcing
climate.title: Logarithmic CO2 forcing approximation
climate.why: A logarithmic approximation connects concentration changes to a forcing perturbation.
climate.limit: User-supplied coefficient; an educational parameterization, not a current assessed forcing product.

climate.name: equilibrium_warming
climate.title: Linear climate response
climate.why: A restoring feedback maps steady forcing to equilibrium temperature change.
climate.limit: Stable linear response with a positive net restoring coefficient.

climate.name: heat_capacity_column
climate.title: Mixed-layer areal heat capacity
climate.why: Mixed-layer depth determines how much energy is needed for warming.
climate.limit: Uniform slab with constant material properties.

climate.name: response_timescale
climate.title: Climate relaxation time
climate.why: Heat storage delays the equilibrium response to forcing.
climate.limit: One-box linear model; output is seconds.

climate.name: step_temperature
climate.title: Transient one-box warming
climate.why: A step forcing exposes the lag between forcing and temperature adjustment.
climate.limit: Zero initial anomaly and constant parameters; no deep-ocean exchange.

climate.name: heat_uptake
climate.title: Areal heat-content change
climate.why: Energy accounting connects warming to ocean heat storage.
climate.limit: One uniform layer; temperature_change is an anomaly.

climate.name: ice_albedo
climate.title: Smooth illustrative ice-albedo transition
climate.why: Temperature-dependent reflection illustrates ice-albedo feedback.
climate.limit: Illustrative smooth closure, not a calibrated satellite albedo retrieval.
climate.extra: require(cold_albedo >= warm_albedo, "cold albedo must be at least warm albedo")

climate.name: carbon_airborne_fraction
climate.title: Carbon budget fraction
climate.why: A carbon mass budget partitions emissions and atmospheric accumulation.
climate.limit: Same time interval and carbon mass units; feedback-driven values above one are not clipped.

climate.name: carbon_decay
climate.title: Single-reservoir carbon relaxation
climate.why: A reservoir model illustrates first-order removal and residence time.
climate.limit: Not a realistic complete atmospheric CO2 impulse response, which has multiple timescales.

climate.name: thermal_expansion_sea_level
climate.title: Steric sea-level slab approximation
climate.why: Ocean expansion connects heat uptake to a sea-level contribution.
climate.limit: Constant coefficient and uniform warming; salinity and pressure dependence are omitted.

climate.name: water_equivalent_sea_level
climate.title: Mass-equivalent sea-level contribution
climate.why: Added ocean water changes mean level through mass conservation.
climate.limit: Uniform ocean area and density; gravitational fingerprints and land motion are omitted.

climate.name: greenhouse_surface_temperature
climate.title: Surface temperature under one absorbing atmospheric layer
climate.why: A layer that absorbs and re-emits infrared returns part of the surface emission and warms the ground.
climate.limit: Blackbody surface, a grey isothermal layer transparent to sunlight; the layer temperature is the surface temperature over 2**0.25.

climate.name: daily_insolation
climate.title: Daily-mean top-of-atmosphere insolation
climate.expr: solar_constant * distance_ratio**2 / np.pi * (h0 * np.sin(latitude) * np.sin(declination) + np.cos(latitude) * np.cos(declination) * np.sin(h0))
climate.why: Latitude, solar declination and Earth-Sun distance set the sunlight a latitude receives over a day.
climate.limit: Declination fixed over the day, no atmosphere; the sunset hour angle h0 is clipped for polar day and night.

climate.name: radiative_convective_temperature
climate.title: Radiative-convective equilibrium temperature profile
climate.why: Convection holds the troposphere at a fixed lapse rate below a radiatively balanced stratosphere.
climate.limit: Grey optically thin stratosphere at the skin temperature; the troposphere passes through the effective temperature at the emission height.

climate.name: equilibrium_solar_constant
climate.title: Solar constant that holds a planet with ice-albedo feedback at a given temperature
climate.expr: 4 * emissivity * SIGMA_SB * temperature**4 / (1 - ice_albedo(temperature, cold_albedo, warm_albedo, transition_temperature, width))
climate.why: Inverting the energy balance traces every equilibrium, including the unstable branch between a warm and an ice-covered state.
climate.limit: Zero-dimensional greybody balance with the ice_albedo closure; equilibria with a negative slope dS/dT are unstable.
climate.extra: require(cold_albedo < 1, "cold albedo must be below one")

climate.name: red_noise_spectrum
climate.title: Temperature spectrum of a one-box climate driven by white noise
climate.why: Heat capacity integrates random weather forcing into slow red-noise climate variability.
climate.limit: Linear one-box model with white-noise forcing; two-sided spectra.

climate.name: methane_forcing
climate.title: Methane radiative forcing (Myhre et al. 1998)
climate.why: Methane forcing grows as a square root of concentration, less the band it shares with nitrous oxide.
climate.limit: Simplified fit to line-by-line calculations, valid near present-day concentrations.

climate.name: nitrous_oxide_forcing
climate.title: Nitrous oxide radiative forcing (Myhre et al. 1998)
climate.why: Nitrous oxide forcing grows as a square root of concentration, less the band it shares with methane.
climate.limit: Simplified fit to line-by-line calculations, valid near present-day concentrations.

climate.name: gregory_regression
climate.title: Forcing and feedback from a regression of imbalance on warming
climate.expr: least squares of imbalance = forcing - restoring * temperature_change
climate.why: In a run with constant forcing, the top-of-atmosphere imbalance falls linearly with warming, so a straight-line fit gives both.
climate.limit: Assumes constant forcing and feedback; returns [forcing W/m^2, restoring W/(m^2 K)].
climate.extra: require(temperature_change.ndim == 1 and temperature_change.size >= 2, "vector of at least two samples")

oceanography.name: hydrostatic_pressure
oceanography.title: Ocean hydrostatic pressure
oceanography.why: Water weight connects pressure and depth.
oceanography.limit: Gauge pressure with constant density; atmospheric pressure is excluded.

oceanography.name: linear_density
oceanography.title: Linear seawater equation of state
oceanography.why: Temperature and salinity both change buoyancy.
oceanography.limit: Local linearization around a supplied reference; not TEOS-10 and no pressure dependence.

oceanography.name: buoyancy_frequency_squared
oceanography.title: Ocean density stratification
oceanography.why: Vertical density gradients control internal oscillations and convection.
oceanography.limit: Coordinate increases upward; negative output denotes unstable stratification.

oceanography.name: geostrophic_current
oceanography.title: Sea-surface geostrophic component
oceanography.why: Sea-surface tilt can reveal large-scale currents.
oceanography.limit: Signed cross-slope component away from the equator; no ageostrophic velocity.

oceanography.name: ekman_transport
oceanography.title: Cross-wind Ekman transport magnitude
oceanography.why: Wind stress and rotation drive vertically integrated transport.
oceanography.limit: Signed cross-wind component per unit width; direction requires a consistent vector convention.

oceanography.name: inertial_period
oceanography.title: Inertial oscillation period
oceanography.why: Rotation supplies a natural timescale for ocean motion.
oceanography.limit: No pressure gradient or friction; invalid at zero Coriolis parameter.

oceanography.name: shallow_wave_speed
oceanography.title: Shallow-water gravity wave
oceanography.why: Long surface waves respond to water depth through gravity.
oceanography.limit: Wavelength much greater than depth, small amplitude, no dispersion.

oceanography.name: deep_wave_speed
oceanography.title: Deep-water phase speed
oceanography.why: Short waves relative to depth propagate dispersively.
oceanography.limit: Deep-water small-amplitude gravity waves without capillarity.

oceanography.name: wave_angular_frequency
oceanography.title: Finite-depth dispersion relation
oceanography.why: The dispersion relation bridges shallow and deep gravity waves.
oceanography.limit: Linear inviscid surface gravity wave, no current or surface tension.

oceanography.name: deep_group_speed
oceanography.title: Deep-water group speed
oceanography.why: Wave energy travels at group speed rather than crest phase speed.
oceanography.limit: Deep-water gravity waves; group speed is half phase speed.

oceanography.name: rossby_radius
oceanography.title: Baroclinic deformation scale
oceanography.why: Stratification and rotation set a horizontal adjustment scale.
oceanography.limit: First-mode constant-N rigid-boundary estimate N H over pi f; not a general layered solution.

oceanography.name: reduced_gravity
oceanography.title: Two-layer reduced gravity
oceanography.why: A small density contrast slows internal waves relative to surface waves.
oceanography.limit: Boussinesq small density contrast; output is acceleration.

oceanography.name: internal_wave_speed
oceanography.title: Two-layer internal long wave
oceanography.why: Layer depths and buoyancy jointly set internal long-wave speed.
oceanography.limit: Hydrostatic two-layer fluid under a rigid lid.

oceanography.name: volume_transport
oceanography.title: Section volume transport
oceanography.why: Integrating velocity over a section produces volume transport.
oceanography.limit: Uniform signed velocity and rectangular section; output m cubed per second, not Sverdrups.

oceanography.name: tidal_elevation
oceanography.title: Single harmonic tide
oceanography.expr: amplitude * np.cos(2 * np.pi * time / period + phase)
oceanography.why: Harmonic constituents provide an inspectable tide representation.
oceanography.limit: One supplied constituent; not a site-specific tide prediction or navigational product.

oceanography.name: gerstner_orbit_radius
oceanography.title: Particle-orbit radius in a Gerstner trochoidal wave
oceanography.why: Water particles in a deep-water wave move on circles that shrink with depth.
oceanography.limit: Exact nonlinear deep-water solution with closed orbits and no Stokes drift; amplitude * wavenumber must not exceed 1.
oceanography.extra: require(amplitude * wavenumber <= 1, "a trochoid steeper than amplitude * wavenumber = 1 overturns")

oceanography.name: ekman_spiral_velocity
oceanography.title: Velocity profile of the Ekman spiral
oceanography.expr: v0 * np.exp(-s) * [np.sin(np.pi / 4 - s), np.sign(coriolis) * np.cos(np.pi / 4 - s)]
oceanography.why: Wind stress diffused downward by friction turns and decays with depth under rotation.
oceanography.limit: Steady, infinitely deep ocean with constant eddy viscosity; last axis holds downwind and crosswind (right of the wind) components.
oceanography.extra: s = depth / np.sqrt(2 * eddy_viscosity / abs(coriolis)); v0 = wind_stress / (density * np.sqrt(eddy_viscosity * abs(coriolis)))

oceanography.name: sverdrup_transport
oceanography.title: Sverdrup meridional transport
oceanography.why: Wind-stress curl drives interior flow across planetary vorticity contours.
oceanography.limit: Steady linear interior balance away from boundaries, friction and the equator; per unit zonal width.

oceanography.name: stommel_streamfunction
oceanography.title: Transport streamfunction of Stommel's wind-driven gyre
oceanography.expr: wind_stress * basin_length / (np.pi * density * friction) * np.sin(np.pi * y / basin_length) * X
oceanography.why: Bottom friction and the beta effect confine the return flow to a western boundary current.
oceanography.limit: Steady linear barotropic vorticity balance in a rectangular basin with psi = 0 on the walls; zonal stress -wind_stress * cos(pi y / basin_length).
oceanography.extra: require(x <= basin_width and y <= basin_length); k = np.pi / basin_length; m1, m2 = (-beta +/- np.sqrt(beta**2 + 4 * friction**2 * k**2)) / (2 * friction); X = 1 + ((np.exp(m2 * L) - 1) * np.exp(m1 * (x - L)) + (np.exp(-m1 * L) - 1) * np.exp(m2 * x)) / (1 - np.exp((m2 - m1) * L)) with L = basin_width

oceanography.name: thermohaline_forcing
oceanography.title: Salt forcing that holds Stommel's two-box overturning steady
oceanography.why: Salt advection by the overturning must balance the freshwater-driven salinity contrast.
oceanography.limit: Temperatures fixed by fast restoring; two stable states coexist for 0 < forcing < thermal_flow**2 / (4 * haline_coefficient).
oceanography.extra: require(flow <= thermal_flow, "flow above thermal_flow implies a negative salinity contrast")

oceanography.name: abyssal_temperature
oceanography.title: Munk's advective-diffusive abyssal temperature profile
oceanography.expr: bottom_temperature + (top_temperature - bottom_temperature) * (np.exp((height - column_height) / h) - np.exp(-column_height / h)) / (1 - np.exp(-column_height / h))
oceanography.why: Slow upwelling balanced by downward mixing of heat sets an exponential thermocline.
oceanography.limit: Steady one-dimensional upwelling-diffusion balance with fixed end temperatures; height measured up from the bottom.
oceanography.extra: h = diffusivity / upwelling; require(height <= column_height, "height must lie inside the column")

oceanography.name: simplified_seawater_density
oceanography.title: Simplified nonlinear seawater density fitted to TEOS-10
oceanography.expr: 1026 - a0 * (1 + lambda1 * t / 2 + mu1 * depth) * t + b0 * (1 - lambda2 * s / 2 - mu2 * depth) * s - nu * t * s
oceanography.why: Cabbeling and thermobaricity make seawater density nonlinear in temperature, salinity and pressure.
oceanography.limit: Roquet et al. (2015) S-EOS with NEMO default coefficients; reproduces TEOS-10 gradients, absolute density off by about 1 kg/m^3.
oceanography.extra: t = conservative_temperature - 283.15; s = absolute_salinity - 35; a0 = 0.16550; b0 = 0.76554; lambda1 = 5.9520e-2; lambda2 = 7.4914e-4; mu1 = 1.4970e-4; mu2 = 1.1090e-5; nu = 2.4341e-3

geophysics.name: sphere_gravity
geophysics.title: Gravitational attraction of a uniform sphere
geophysics.why: A compact body with excess density pulls a plumb line sideways and adds to gravity above it.
geophysics.limit: Observer outside the sphere, which attracts as a point mass; last axis holds the horizontal (toward +x) and downward components.
geophysics.extra: M = 4 / 3 * np.pi * radius**3 * density_contrast; require(x**2 + depth**2 >= radius**2)

geophysics.name: bouguer_correction
geophysics.title: Attraction of an infinite horizontal slab
geophysics.why: Rock between the station and the reference level adds gravity that does not depend on the slab's extent.
geophysics.limit: Flat, uniform, laterally infinite slab; no terrain or curvature correction.

geophysics.name: free_air_correction
geophysics.title: Free-air gravity correction
geophysics.why: Gravity falls off with distance from the Earth's centre, about 0.3086 mGal per metre at the surface.
geophysics.limit: First order in height / radius for a spherical point-mass Earth; no rock between station and reference.

geophysics.name: bouguer_anomaly
geophysics.title: Simple Bouguer gravity anomaly
geophysics.expr: observed_gravity - normal_gravity + 2 * normal_gravity * height / radius - 2 * np.pi * G * density * height
geophysics.why: Removing latitude, height and the rock slab under a station leaves the attraction of buried density contrasts.
geophysics.limit: Free-air and infinite-slab reductions only, without terrain correction.

geophysics.name: torsion_balance_gravitational_constant
geophysics.title: Gravitational constant from a torsion balance
geophysics.why: The twist of a suspended rod between large masses, timed by its free swing, measures G.
geophysics.limit: Point masses, a massless rod and attraction by the near large ball only.

geophysics.name: earth_mean_density
geophysics.title: Mean density of the Earth
geophysics.why: Surface gravity and the gravitational constant together weigh the Earth.
geophysics.limit: Spherically symmetric, nonrotating Earth; gravitational_constant defaults to constants.G.

geophysics.name: centrifugal_ratio
geophysics.title: Ratio of centrifugal to gravitational acceleration at the equator
geophysics.why: Rotation flattens a planet in proportion to how strongly it competes with gravity.
geophysics.limit: Equatorial ratio with surface gravity; the geodetic m uses GM / (a b) instead.

geophysics.name: homogeneous_flattening
geophysics.title: Flattening of a slowly rotating homogeneous fluid planet
geophysics.why: A uniform self-gravitating fluid in rotation settles into an oblate spheroid.
geophysics.limit: First order in rotation (Maclaurin spheroid); centrifugal_ratio at most 0.1.

geophysics.name: clairaut_gravity
geophysics.title: Gravity on a rotating spheroid from Clairaut's theorem
geophysics.why: The increase of gravity toward the poles measures the flattening without any surveying.
geophysics.limit: First order in flattening and rotation for a hydrostatic spheroid; no sin^4 term.

geophysics.name: normal_gravity
geophysics.title: Normal gravity on the GRS80 ellipsoid
geophysics.expr: gamma_e * (1 + k * np.sin(latitude) ** 2) / np.sqrt(1 - e2 * np.sin(latitude) ** 2)
geophysics.why: The reference field that gravity anomalies are measured against.
geophysics.limit: Somigliana's closed form on the GRS80 ellipsoid surface.

geophysics.name: flattening_from_j2
geophysics.title: Flattening of a hydrostatic Earth from its J2
geophysics.why: The oblateness term of the gravity field and the rotation fix the shape of the level surface.
geophysics.limit: First order in flattening; second-order terms change 1/f by about 0.1%.

geophysics.name: nodal_precession_rate
geophysics.title: Secular regression of a satellite orbit's node
geophysics.why: The equatorial bulge torques an inclined orbit, so the node drifts at a rate that measures J2.
geophysics.limit: First-order secular J2 perturbation without drag or higher harmonics; perigee above the reference radius.
geophysics.extra: n = np.sqrt(gravitational_parameter / semi_major_axis**3); require(semi_major_axis * (1 - eccentricity) > radius)

geophysics.name: stokes_function
geophysics.title: Stokes's kernel for the geoid
geophysics.expr: 1 / s - 6 * s + 1 - 5 * np.cos(psi) - 3 * np.cos(psi) * np.log(s + s**2)
geophysics.why: Weighting gravity anomalies over the whole globe by spherical distance gives the geoid height.
geophysics.limit: Spherical approximation with no masses outside the geoid; singular at zero distance.

geophysics.name: degree_geoid_height
geophysics.title: Geoid height of one spherical-harmonic degree of the gravity anomaly
geophysics.why: Stokes's integral divides each degree of the anomaly by n - 1, so long wavelengths dominate the geoid.
geophysics.limit: Spherical approximation of Stokes's formula for degrees of at least 2.
geophysics.extra: require(degree == np.round(degree), "degree must be an integer")

geophysics.name: dipole_field
geophysics.title: Field of a geocentric axial dipole
geophysics.why: A uniformly magnetized Earth gives a field that dips more steeply toward the poles.
geophysics.limit: Pure axial dipole outside its sources; last axis holds the northward and downward components.

geophysics.name: dipole_inclination
geophysics.title: Inclination of an axial dipole field
geophysics.why: The dip of a compass needle tells a navigator, or a rock, its magnetic latitude.
geophysics.limit: Geocentric axial dipole; positive downward for today's polarity.

geophysics.name: paleolatitude
geophysics.title: Paleolatitude from a remanent inclination
geophysics.why: A rock's frozen-in dip records how far from the pole it formed.
geophysics.limit: Geocentric axial dipole averaged over secular variation.

geophysics.name: zonal_field
geophysics.title: Field of one zonal Gauss coefficient
geophysics.expr: (a / r) ** (n + 2) * coefficient * [lpmv(1, n, x), -(n + 1) * lpmv(0, n, x)]
geophysics.why: Expanding the potential in spherical harmonics separates the dipole from smaller, faster-decaying parts.
geophysics.limit: Internal zonal sources only; last axis holds the northward and downward components.
geophysics.extra: x = np.sin(latitude); a = reference_radius; r = distance; n = degree; require(degree == np.round(degree), "degree must be an integer")

geophysics.name: gauss_dipole_moment
geophysics.title: Dipole moment from the degree-1 Gauss coefficients
geophysics.expr: 4 * np.pi * reference_radius**3 / MU0 * np.sqrt(g10**2 + g11**2 + h11**2)
geophysics.why: Gauss's analysis weighed the Earth's magnet from surface measurements alone.
geophysics.limit: Magnitude of the best-fitting geocentric tilted dipole.

geophysics.name: field_elements
geophysics.title: Declination, inclination and intensity of a field vector
geophysics.expr: [np.arctan2(east, north), np.arctan2(down, np.hypot(north, east)), np.sqrt(north**2 + east**2 + down**2)]
geophysics.why: Magnetic directions in rocks and observatories are reported as two angles and a strength.
geophysics.limit: Local north-east-down frame; the field vector must be nonzero.
geophysics.extra: require(intensity > 0, "the field vector must be nonzero")

geophysics.name: direction_angle
geophysics.title: Angle between two magnetic directions
geophysics.expr: np.arccos(np.sin(Ia) * np.sin(Ib) + np.cos(Ia) * np.cos(Ib) * np.cos(Da - Db))
geophysics.why: A remanence more than 90 degrees from the present field records a reversed polarity.
geophysics.limit: Great-circle distance between unit vectors; intensities are ignored.

geophysics.name: virtual_geomagnetic_pole
geophysics.title: Virtual geomagnetic pole of a site direction
geophysics.expr: [np.arctan2(z, np.hypot(x, y)), np.arctan2(y, x)] of site * np.cos(p) + (north * np.cos(D) + east * np.sin(D)) * np.sin(p)
geophysics.why: Poles from rocks of one age on one continent should agree; when they wander, the continent moved.
geophysics.limit: Geocentric dipole pole; last axis holds pole latitude and longitude in [0, 2 pi).
geophysics.extra: p = np.arctan2(2 * np.cos(I), np.sin(I)); site, north, east are the site unit vector and its local north and east unit vectors

geophysics.name: block_magnetic_anomaly
geophysics.title: Magnetic anomaly of a vertically magnetized two-dimensional block
geophysics.why: Strips of normally and reversely magnetized crust give the alternating anomalies over mid-ocean ridges.
geophysics.limit: Infinite strike, vertical magnetization and ambient field (reduced to the pole); left < right and top < bottom.
geophysics.extra: phi(z) = np.arctan((right - x) / z) - np.arctan((left - x) / z); require(left < right); require(top < bottom)

geophysics.name: magnetic_reynolds_number
geophysics.title: Magnetic Reynolds number
geophysics.why: A conducting fluid can stretch and regenerate a magnetic field only if advection beats diffusion.
geophysics.limit: Order-of-magnitude scale; dynamos need values above a threshold of order 10 to 100.

geophysics.name: magnetic_decay_time
geophysics.title: Free decay time of the slowest magnetic mode of a conducting sphere
geophysics.why: Without a dynamo the Earth's field would die in tens of thousands of years, far less than its age.
geophysics.limit: Uniform stationary conductor surrounded by an insulator.

geophysics.name: rikitake_fixed_point
geophysics.title: Steady state of Rikitake's two-disc dynamo
geophysics.why: The two coupled discs have a pair of steady states of opposite polarity, which the chaotic flow visits in turn.
geophysics.limit: Positive state of the nondimensional Rikitake system; the other is (-x, -y, z).

geophysics.name: love_number_h2
geophysics.title: Degree-2 displacement Love number of a homogeneous elastic Earth
geophysics.why: The solid Earth rises and falls with the tide by a fraction of the equilibrium tide that measures its rigidity.
geophysics.limit: Uniform incompressible self-gravitating elastic sphere (Kelvin's solution).

geophysics.name: love_number_k2
geophysics.title: Degree-2 potential Love number of a homogeneous elastic Earth
geophysics.why: The tidal bulge adds its own gravitational potential, a fraction k2 of the tidal potential.
geophysics.limit: Uniform incompressible self-gravitating elastic sphere; the fluid limit is 3/2.

geophysics.name: tidal_gravimetric_factor
geophysics.title: Gravimetric factor of the body tide
geophysics.why: A gravimeter on a yielding Earth sees the tide amplified by its uplift and reduced by the bulge's attraction.
geophysics.limit: Degree-2 tide on a spherically symmetric elastic Earth without ocean loading.

geophysics.name: equivalent_water_height
geophysics.title: Water layer behind a change of one Stokes coefficient
geophysics.expr: radius * mean_density * (2 * degree + 1) * coefficient_change / (3 * water_density * (1 + load_love_number))
geophysics.why: Monthly gravity fields from a satellite pair reveal the moving mass of water, ice and groundwater.
geophysics.limit: Thin surface layer on an elastic Earth (Wahr et al., 1998), fully normalized coefficients.
geophysics.extra: require(degree == np.round(degree), "degree must be an integer")

volcanology.name: decay_constant
volcanology.title: Decay constant from a half-life
volcanology.why: Every radioactive nuclide has a fixed probability per unit time of decaying, set by its half-life.
volcanology.limit: Rutherford and Soddy (1902): first-order decay, independent of temperature, pressure and chemistry.

volcanology.name: parent_fraction
volcanology.title: Fraction of radioactive parent atoms remaining
volcanology.why: Exponential decay is the clock behind every radiometric age.
volcanology.limit: Rutherford and Soddy (1902): a closed system with no parent added after time zero.

volcanology.name: radiometric_age
volcanology.title: Age from a radiogenic daughter-to-parent ratio

params.name: daughter_parent_ratio
params.unit: 1, radiogenic daughter atoms per parent atom

volcanology.why: The ratio of accumulated daughter atoms to surviving parent atoms grows with time, so measuring it dates the rock.
volcanology.limit: Closed system with no initial daughter; Boltwood (1907) applied it to lead in uranium minerals.

volcanology.name: radiogenic_daughter
volcanology.title: Radiogenic daughter accumulated beside the surviving parent

params.name: parent
params.unit: Surviving parent amount today (atoms, moles or any consistent unit)

volcanology.why: Forward accumulation shows how the daughter-to-parent ratio of a rock records its age.
volcanology.limit: Closed system with no initial daughter; the inverse of radiometric_age. Holmes (1913) used it to build the first radiometric time scale.

volcanology.name: radiocarbon_age
volcanology.title: Conventional radiocarbon age

params.name: fraction_modern
params.unit: 1, sample 14C/12C relative to the modern standard

volcanology.why: Living matter exchanges carbon-14 with the atmosphere; after death the carbon-14 decays, dating organic remains.
volcanology.limit: Libby et al. (1949) with the conventional 5568-year (Libby) half-life, mean life LIBBY_MEAN_LIFE; it is a radiocarbon age, not a calendar age, until calibrated.

volcanology.name: radiogenic_lead_ratio
volcanology.title: Radiogenic 207Pb/206Pb ratio produced over a given age
volcanology.why: Two uranium isotopes decaying at different rates make the ratio of their lead daughters a clock that needs no uranium measurement.
volcanology.limit: Patterson (1956): closed system with today's 238U/235U = U238_U235 and the Jaffey et al. (1971) decay constants. The ratio tends to LAMBDA_U235 / (U238_U235 * LAMBDA_U238) at zero age.

volcanology.name: lead_lead_age
volcanology.title: Age from a radiogenic 207Pb/206Pb ratio

params.name: lead_ratio
params.unit: 1, radiogenic 207Pb*/206Pb* or the slope of a Pb-Pb isochron
params.kind: between the ratios at one year (about 0.0461) and at 10 Ga

volcanology.why: Patterson dated the Earth from the slope of a meteorite lead isochron, which equals this ratio.
volcanology.limit: Inverts radiogenic_lead_ratio by Brent's method between one year and 10 Ga; same closed-system assumptions.
volcanology.extra: require(radiogenic_lead_ratio(1 year) <= lead_ratio <= radiogenic_lead_ratio(10 Ga)); solved with brentq

volcanology.name: concordia_ratios
volcanology.title: Point on the Wetherill U-Pb concordia
volcanology.why: Both uranium-lead clocks agree only on this curve, so a zircon off it has lost lead and its chord dates the loss.
volcanology.limit: Wetherill (1956): closed system with the Jaffey et al. (1971) decay constants. Episodic lead loss puts samples on a straight chord (discordia) between the concordia points of formation and loss.

volcanology.name: isochron_fit
volcanology.title: Age and initial ratio from a whole-rock or mineral isochron

params.name: parent_ratio
params.unit: 1, parent over a stable reference isotope (e.g. 87Rb/86Sr)

params.name: daughter_ratio
params.unit: 1, daughter over the same reference isotope (e.g. 87Sr/86Sr)

volcanology.why: Cogenetic minerals with different parent contents line up on a straight line whose slope gives the age without knowing the initial daughter.
volcanology.limit: Nicolaysen (1961): every sample formed at the same time with the same initial ratio and stayed closed; ordinary least squares without measurement-error weighting (a York fit would weight them). The slope must be positive.
volcanology.extra: require(slope > 0); parent_ratio must vary and match daughter_ratio

volcanology.name: rayleigh_fractionation
volcanology.title: Isotope ratio of a reservoir depleted by Rayleigh distillation

params.name: initial_ratio
params.unit: 1, heavy-to-light isotope ratio of the reservoir at the start

params.name: fractionation_factor
params.unit: 1, product ratio over reservoir ratio at each instant

volcanology.why: Removing a product that is always slightly enriched in one isotope drives the remaining reservoir further and further from its starting composition.
volcanology.limit: Rayleigh (1896): the product leaves as soon as it forms, the reservoir stays well mixed and the factor is constant.

volcanology.name: delta_value
volcanology.title: Isotope delta value relative to a standard

params.name: ratio
params.unit: 1, heavy-to-light isotope ratio of the sample

params.name: standard_ratio
params.unit: 1, the same ratio in the standard (e.g. VSMOW, VPDB)

volcanology.why: Isotope ratios vary in the fourth decimal place, so geochemists report deviations from a standard in per mil.
volcanology.limit: Linear in the ratio; delta values of different standards must be converted before they are compared.

volcanology.name: fractional_crystallization_melt
volcanology.title: Trace-element concentration in a melt during fractional crystallization

params.name: initial_concentration
params.unit: Concentration in the parent melt (any unit, e.g. ppm)

volcanology.why: Crystals removed as soon as they form leave the residual melt enriched in the elements they reject.
volcanology.limit: Rayleigh fractional crystallization (Bowen 1928; Gast 1968): crystals do not re-equilibrate and the bulk partition coefficient is constant.

volcanology.name: equilibrium_crystallization_melt
volcanology.title: Trace-element concentration in a melt during equilibrium crystallization

params.name: initial_concentration
params.unit: Concentration in the parent melt (any unit, e.g. ppm)

volcanology.why: Crystals that keep reacting with the melt, as in Bowen's continuous series, limit how far the melt can evolve.
volcanology.limit: Batch mass balance (Shaw 1970): solid and melt stay in equilibrium, so an incompatible element is enriched at most by 1 / partition_coefficient.

volcanology.name: lattice_strain_partition
volcanology.title: Mineral-melt partition coefficient from the strain of the crystal lattice

params.name: optimal_radius
params.unit: m, radius that fits the site without strain

params.name: peak_partition
params.unit: 1, partition coefficient of an ion of the optimal radius

params.name: youngs_modulus
params.unit: Pa, apparent Young's modulus of the site

volcanology.expr: peak_partition * np.exp(-4 * np.pi * youngs_modulus * AVOGADRO * (optimal_radius / 2 * (ionic_radius - optimal_radius)**2 + (ionic_radius - optimal_radius)**3 / 3) / (R_GAS * temperature))
volcanology.why: Ions close in size to the site they replace enter a crystal easily, which is Goldschmidt's first rule of substitution.
volcanology.limit: Blundy and Wood (1994) quantification of Goldschmidt (1937) for isovalent ions on one site; charge differences need a separate parabola.

volcanology.name: isotope_temperature
volcanology.title: Calcite-water oxygen-isotope paleotemperature

params.name: delta_calcite
params.unit: per mil, delta18O of the carbonate (CO2 from the calcite, PDB scale)

params.name: delta_water
params.unit: per mil, delta18O of the water on the same scale

volcanology.why: The oxygen-isotope fractionation between a shell and the water it grew in falls with temperature, so fossil shells record ancient ocean temperatures.
volcanology.limit: Urey (1947) predicted the effect; this is the empirical calibration of Epstein, Buchsbaum, Lowenstam and Urey (1953), valid for about 7-30 degC and equilibrium calcite.

volcanology.name: arrhenius_viscosity
volcanology.title: Arrhenius temperature dependence of melt viscosity

params.name: reference_viscosity
params.unit: Pa s, viscosity at the reference temperature

volcanology.why: Silicate melts stiffen by orders of magnitude as they cool, which controls how lava flows and how magma erupts.
volcanology.limit: Constant activation energy over the range of interest; crystal- and bubble-free Newtonian melt.

volcanology.name: shaw_viscosity
volcanology.title: Shaw's empirical viscosity of an anhydrous or hydrous silicate melt

params.name: slope
params.unit: 1, Shaw's s from the molar composition (about 2-3 for basalt, 3.5-4 for rhyolite)

volcanology.why: One composition-dependent slope predicts the viscosity of melts from basalt to rhyolite.
volcanology.limit: Shaw (1972), Am. J. Sci. 272: 870-893; all lines pass near ln(eta [poise]) = -6.4 at 1e4/T = 1.5. Crystal- and bubble-free Newtonian melt; about 0.2 log units of accuracy.

volcanology.name: water_solubility
volcanology.title: Dissolved water in a melt saturated at a given pressure

params.name: solubility_constant
params.unit: 1/sqrt(Pa), mass fraction per root pascal (about 4.1e-6 for rhyolite)

volcanology.why: Water dissolves as hydroxyl, so its solubility grows as the square root of pressure and ascending magma exsolves bubbles.
volcanology.limit: Square-root (Henry-type) law for pure water vapour, valid up to a few hundred MPa; ignores CO2 and temperature.

volcanology.name: dike_ascent_velocity
volcanology.title: Mean laminar velocity of buoyant magma in a dike
volcanology.why: Buoyancy drives magma up a planar crack, and the viscous drag on its walls sets how fast it rises.
volcanology.limit: Wilson and Head (1981): plane Poiseuille flow between parallel walls driven by buoyancy alone; check that the Reynolds number ``magma_density * velocity * width / viscosity`` stays below about 2000.

volcanology.name: mogi_displacement
volcanology.title: Surface displacement above an inflating point source

params.name: radial_distance
params.unit: m, horizontal distance from the point above the source

params.name: volume_change
params.unit: m^3, signed change of the source volume

volcanology.why: Magma entering a chamber lifts the ground in a bell-shaped dome whose width reveals the chamber depth.
volcanology.limit: Mogi (1958) point source in an elastic half-space; the chamber radius must be small compared with its depth. The uplift halves at ``radial_distance = 0.766 * depth``.

volcanology.name: plume_rise_height
volcanology.title: Maximum height of a buoyant plume in a stratified fluid

params.name: buoyancy_flux
params.unit: m^4/s^3, source ``reduced_gravity * velocity * radius**2`` (the factor pi omitted)

volcanology.why: Turbulent entrainment dilutes a plume until the stratification removes its buoyancy, which caps its height at a value set by only the source buoyancy flux and the stratification.
volcanology.limit: Morton, Taylor and Turner (1956) for a steady point source of buoyancy in uniform stratification, with Briggs's constant 5.0 (entrainment about 0.1); source momentum, wind and moisture are neglected.

volcanology.name: column_height
volcanology.title: Height of a Plinian eruption column from its heat flux

params.name: heat_flux
params.unit: W, rate of heat release ``mass_eruption_rate * specific_heat * temperature_excess``

volcanology.why: The thermal energy released at the vent, not the eruption velocity, controls how high a volcanic column rises.
volcanology.limit: Wilson, Sparks, Huang and Watkins (1978), JGR 83: 1829-1836, for a standard atmosphere and a strong steady column; wind bends weak plumes lower.

volcanology.name: volcanic_explosivity_index
volcanology.title: Volcanic Explosivity Index from the erupted tephra volume
volcanology.why: A single logarithmic number lets eruptions of very different style and size be compared and catalogued.
volcanology.limit: Newhall and Self (1982), volume criterion only: VEI 0 below 1e4 m^3, 1 below 1e6 m^3, then one step per factor of ten up to VEI 8 at 1e12 m^3 and above. Column height and other criteria are not used.
